newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Higher peso seen slowing down Manila wheat buying.
newsitem.headline: Higher peso seen slowing down Manila wheat buying.

text.p: Manila wheat importers are expected to trek back to the market this week but analysts said a weaker peso and firmer U.S. prices would limit orders, Manila grains traders said on Monday.
"I'm waiting for prices to dip. If the figures are right I will buy," an executive in a local flour mill told Reuters.
"Everybody's on close watch due to the double whammy from the drop of the peso and the rise of wheat prices due to drier weather outlook on the U.S. corn crop," he added.
Most Philippine wheat buyers ran away from the market last week after the peso dropped by 11.5 percent to 29.45 on July 11. The peso has seen recovered to 28 pesos to a dollar.

Philippine wheat buyers currently buy U.S. spring wheat at an average $187 per tonne FOB compared to less than $180 before the peso was effectively devalued and western white wheat at $148 per tonne FOB from $140.
But despite higher prices some mills made orders last week to meet short term requirements.

Traders said Philippine mills bought 18,500 tonnes western white wheat at $142 to $143 per tonne FOB, 8,000 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat with 13.5 percent protein content at $181 to $182 per tonne FOB, and 13,500 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat with 14 percent protein content at $186 to $187 per tonne FOB.
Rice, corn and soybean importers are expected to remain absent in the market due to ample supplies.
Philippine importers shrugged off reports Egypt has banned the import of genetically engineered grain.

"All of these things are thought of in anticipation of the use of genetic engineering in wheat production," said an executive in a local flour mill. "But unless we know the effect of genetically engineered wheat to human and the environment its premature to say anything about it."
